A <search> with search-bar on it is the bar: a leading icon or icon button, an <input type="search">, and whatever trailing actions the query needs. The element is the landmark — there is no role="search" to add.

search {% call code() %} search {% endcall %}

The input carries none of the text-field chrome — no underline, no floating label, no container of its own. The bar is the container, so the input goes in bare rather than inside a .field.

Spacing follows what is at each end: a bare glyph sits 16dp from the edge, an icon button 4dp, because the button already insets its own glyph by 12dp. Nothing to set — the bar reads its own children.

.searchbar, the pre-1.0 name, still reaches the same rules.

{% endcall %} {% call section("leading-action", "A leading action") %}

When the bar opens a drawer or goes back, the leading glyph becomes an icon button. The bar closes up around it on its own.

{% call code() %} {% endcall %}

An <img> in the bar is the account avatar M3 puts in that slot — 30dp and circular. Put it inside the button when it is tappable, so the 48dp target comes from the button.

{% endcall %} {% call section("docked", "Docked view") %}

The docked view is a .search-view inside the bar. It hangs off the bar, so the bar keeps its position: relative and the view needs no coordinates of its own. Show and hide it with the hidden attribute.

It is a plain element rather than a <dialog> on purpose: dialog.show() moves focus into the dialog, which would take the caret out of the input the user is typing in.

The demo below starts open so the surface is on the page; the sample under it has the hidden a real page would write. Focus the input to reopen it.

Full screen, the view is a <dialog> opened with showModal(). Escape and a tap outside come from the platform, so there is nothing to wire up beyond opening it. Its header is another .search-bar — same markup, with the pill and the shadow taken off.

 {% endcall %}

Full screen below 600px and docked above it is the M3 rule of thumb. Both variants are the same markup, so a page can render one and let the window size pick.

{% endcall %} {% call section("suggestions", "Suggestions are Autocomplete") %}

Search does not ship a suggestion list of its own. Put autocomplete on the bar's input and you get the combobox, its listbox, and the arrow-key and aria-activedescendant handling that Autocomplete already implements and is tested for.

{% call code() %} search {% endcall %} {% call code() %} Expressive.Autocomplete.init(document.querySelector('.search-bar input'), { minLength: 0, data: [{ id: 'Apricot' }, { id: 'Blackcurrant' }, { id: 'Clementine' }] }); {% endcall %}

That is the whole relationship, and it is deliberate. A .search-view takes no composite role: its contents are links and buttons reached with Tab, and a second listbox here would be the same promise as Autocomplete's with no keyboard model behind it. Use the view for recent searches, filters, and results; use Autocomplete for a list the user arrows through.
